ENVIRONMENT
- C++ reference binary (ground truth): /workspace/dataset/test11_executable
- Rust port under test:                /output/test11
- Rust source lives in /output (test11.rs, src/lib.rs, src/idna/*.rs). You may READ it.
- The C++ library source (idna.hpp / idna.cpp) does NOT exist on disk. Do not look for it.

HARD RULES
- You MUST NOT modify, create, or delete anything under /output. Read-only there.
- Do all scratch work under your own private scratch dir; create it with
  mkdir -p and use a path unique to you (given below). Never write to /tmp root directly.
- Both binaries take the SAME argv. Compare raw bytes of stdout AND the exit code.
- Compare with byte-exact tooling (cmp, or diff on files, or shell string equality on
  command substitution ONLY when you know there are no trailing-newline subtleties).
  Prefer writing stdout to files and using 'cmp -s'.
- Arguments may contain spaces, quotes, newlines, NUL-adjacent bytes, and invalid UTF-8.
  Quote your shell variables properly ("$x", not $x).
- Report ONLY real, reproduced divergences. If you cannot reproduce it twice, it is not
  a finding. Do not speculate about code you did not execute.

Your private scratch dir: /tmp/wf-fuzz-r1-3

TASK — differential fuzzing, round 1, strategy "ace-prefix".

Your assigned angle:
The "xn--" prefix in every mutation: exact, upper/mixed case (XN--, Xn--, xN--), truncated (x, xn, xn-), repeated (xn--xn--xn--), embedded mid-string, per-label (a.xn--b), prefix-only, prefix plus one char, and "xn--" with trailing dots.

Write a shell (or python3) driver in your scratch dir that, for each generated input,
runs both binaries with that input as a single argv element, captures stdout to
separate files, and compares them with 'cmp -s'. Also compare exit codes. Print only
the mismatches, plus a final total of cases executed.

Generate inputs PROGRAMMATICALLY so you can cover hundreds to thousands of cases.
Use printf with escapes (e.g. printf '\xff') or python3 to build byte sequences, and
pass them via a shell array or python subprocess with a list argv — never by
re-splitting a string. python3 + subprocess.run([...], capture_output=True) with
bytes arguments (os.fsencode / bytes objects) is the most reliable route for
arbitrary bytes; prefer it.



Report every reproduced divergence with an exact repro command. If you find none,
say so honestly with divergenceCount 0 — a clean result is a useful result, and
inventing a finding is much worse than reporting none. In notes, state what you
deliberately did NOT cover so a later reviewer can pick it up.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Differential fuzzer, round 1, strategy "ace-prefix".

Focuses every mutation on the "xn--" ACE prefix: exact, case variants,
truncations, repetitions, embedded, per-label, prefix-only, prefix+1 char,
and prefix with trailing dots.

Each input is passed as a SINGLE argv element (bytes) to both binaries.
stdout is captured to bytes and compared byte-exactly; exit codes compared too.
"""

import itertools
import subprocess
import sys

CPP = "/workspace/dataset/test11_executable"
RUST = "/output/test11"


def bash_ansi_c(b: bytes) -> str:
    """Fully hex-escaped bash $'...' literal: exact for every byte but NUL."""
    return "$'" + "".join("\\x%02x" % c for c in b) + "'"


def repro(args: list) -> str:
    q = " ".join(bash_ansi_c(a) for a in args)
    return "%s %s   # vs:  %s %s" % (CPP, q, RUST, q)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- generation


def gen_prefix_variants():
    """Every case permutation and truncation / dash mutation of 'xn--'."""
    out = []
    # all 4 case permutations of the two letters, crossed with dash counts 0..5
    for xs in ("x", "X"):
        for ns in ("n", "N"):
            for dashes in range(0, 6):
                out.append((xs + ns + "-" * dashes).encode())
    # single-letter truncations
    for t in ("", "x", "X", "n", "N", "-", "--", "---", "----"):
        out.append(t.encode())
    # letter-only truncations with a dash in odd places
    for t in ("x-n--", "-xn--", "x-n-", "xn.-", "xn_-", "xn -", "x n--",
              "xnn--", "xxn--", "xn--x", "xn--n", "xn---x", "nx--", "-n--",
              "x--", "xn+-", "xn=-", "xn––", "ｘｎ--"):
        out.append(t.encode())
    # bytes that are *almost* x/n
    for t in (b"\x78\x6e\x2d\x2d", b"\x78\x6e\x2d", b"\xf8n--", b"x\xee--",
              b"\x78\x4e\x2d\x2d", b"xn\x2d\xad", b"xn--\xff", b"\xffxn--"):
        out.append(t)
    # dedupe, keep order
    seen, uniq = set(), []
    for p in out:
        if p not in seen:
            seen.add(p)
            uniq.append(p)
    return uniq


BODIES = [
    b"",
    b"a",
    b"ab",
    b"A",
    b"AB",
    b"Z",
    b"0",
    b"-",
    b".",
    b"..",
    b"...",
    b"a.b",
    b"a..b",
    b".a",
    b"a.",
    b"example.com",
    b"EXAMPLE.COM",
    b"ExAmPlE.CoM",
    b"xn--a",
    b"xn--",
    b"XN--a",
    b"\xe6\x97\xa5\xe6\x9c\xac\xe8\xaa\x9e",          # 日本語
    b"\xe4\xb8\xad\xe5\x9b\xbd.cn",                    # 中国.cn
    b"\xff",
    b"\xff\xfe",
    b"\x80",
    b"\x7f",
    b"\xc3",                                            # truncated UTF-8 lead
    b"\xed\xa0\x80",                                    # surrogate (invalid)
    b"\xf4\x90\x80\x80",                                # > U+10FFFF
    b"\n",
    b"\r\n",
    b"\t",
    b" ",
    b"  a  ",
    b'"',
    b"'",
    b"\\",
    b"a\nb",
    b"a b",
    b"a\tb",
    b"a" * 59,
    b"a" * 60,
    b"a" * 63,
    b"a" * 64,
    b"a" * 251,
    b"a" * 252,
    b"A" * 255,
    b"a" * 256,
]


def gen_cases():
    """Yield (tag, [argv bytes...]) pairs."""
    prefixes = gen_prefix_variants()

    # 1. prefix alone
    for p in prefixes:
        yield ("prefix-only", [p])

    # 2. prefix + body  (the big cross product)
    for p in prefixes:
        for b in BODIES:
            yield ("prefix+body", [p + b])

    # 3. prefix + exactly one char (incl. non-ASCII / control single bytes)
    one_chars = [bytes([c]) for c in (
        0x01, 0x09, 0x0a, 0x0d, 0x20, 0x21, 0x2d, 0x2e, 0x2f, 0x30, 0x3a,
        0x41, 0x5a, 0x5f, 0x61, 0x7a, 0x7e, 0x7f, 0x80, 0xc0, 0xed, 0xfe, 0xff)]
    for p in prefixes:
        for c in one_chars:
            yield ("prefix+1char", [p + c])

    # 4. repeated prefixes 1..8, each case flavour, with and without a tail
    for flavour in (b"xn--", b"XN--", b"Xn--", b"xN--", b"xn-", b"xn", b"x"):
        for n in range(1, 9):
            base = flavour * n
            yield ("repeat", [base])
            yield ("repeat", [base + b"a"])
            yield ("repeat", [base + b"example.com"])
            yield ("repeat", [base + b"\xe6\x97\xa5"])
            yield ("repeat", [b"a" + base])
            yield ("repeat", [base + b"."])

    # 5. embedded mid-string at every offset of a small carrier
    carriers = [b"abcdef", b"a.b.c", b"....", b"AB.CD", b"\xff\xff\xff"]
    for p in (b"xn--", b"XN--", b"xn-", b"xn", b"Xn--", b"xN--"):
        for carrier in carriers:
            for i in range(len(carrier) + 1):
                yield ("embedded", [carrier[:i] + p + carrier[i:]])

    # 6. per-label placement
    label_sets = [
        b"a.%s b", b"a.%sb", b"%sa.b", b"a.b.%sc", b"%s.%s", b"a.%s.b",
        b"%sa.%sb", b"a.b.c.%s", b"%s.a.%s.b.%s",
    ]
    for p in (b"xn--", b"XN--", b"Xn--", b"xN--", b"xn-", b"xn", b"x", b""):
        for tmpl in label_sets:
            n = tmpl.count(b"%s")
            try:
                yield ("per-label", [tmpl % tuple([p] * n)])
            except TypeError:
                pass

    # 7. prefix with trailing dots (and leading dots)
    for p in (b"xn--", b"XN--", b"Xn--", b"xN--", b"xn-", b"xn", b"x", b"xn---",
              b"xn--xn--"):
        for nd in range(0, 9):
            dots = b"." * nd
            yield ("trailing-dots", [p + dots])
            yield ("trailing-dots", [dots + p])
            yield ("trailing-dots", [dots + p + dots])
            yield ("trailing-dots", [p + dots + b"a"])
            yield ("trailing-dots", [p + b"a" + dots])

    # 8. length boundaries with the prefix consuming part of the budget
    for p in (b"xn--", b"XN--", b"xn-", b"xn", b""):
        for total in (0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 62, 63, 64, 65, 253, 254, 255, 256, 257):
            pad = total - len(p)
            if pad < 0:
                continue
            yield ("length", [p + b"a" * pad])
            yield ("length", [p + b"\xe6\x97\xa5" * (pad // 3) + b"a" * (pad % 3)])

    # 9. prefix glued to invalid UTF-8 and to combining/zero-width chars
    exotic = [
        b"\xe2\x80\x8b",              # ZWSP
        b"\xef\xbb\xbf",              # BOM
        b"\xcc\x81",                  # combining acute
        b"\xc2\xad",                  # soft hyphen
        b"\xe3\x80\x82",              # ideographic full stop
        b"\xef\xbc\x8e",              # fullwidth full stop
        b"\xf0\x9f\x92\xa9",          # emoji
        b"\xc0\x80",                  # overlong NUL
        b"\xf7\xbf\xbf\xbf",
        b"\xfe\xff",
    ]
    for p in (b"xn--", b"XN--", b"xn-", b"xn"):
        for e in exotic:
            yield ("exotic", [p + e])
            yield ("exotic", [e + p])
            yield ("exotic", [p + e + p])
            yield ("exotic", [p + e + b"a"])

    # 10. every single byte (1..255) appended to and prepended to "xn--"
    for c in range(1, 256):
        yield ("bytesweep", [b"xn--" + bytes([c])])
        yield ("bytesweep", [bytes([c]) + b"xn--"])
        yield ("bytesweep", [b"xn-" + bytes([c]) + b"a"])
        yield ("bytesweep", [b"x" + bytes([c]) + b"n--a"])

    # 11. multi-argv: several xn-- flavours at once (multi-line output)
    multi = [
        [b"xn--a", b"XN--a"],
        [b"xn--", b"xn--", b"xn--"],
        [b"xn--\xff", b"\xffxn--", b"xn--."],
        [b"", b"xn--", b""],
        [b"xn--" * 3, b"a.xn--b", b"xn--..."],
        [b"xn--a"] * 12,
    ]
    for m in multi:
        yield ("multi-argv", m)

    # 12. the no-argument default path
    yield ("no-args", [])


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- execution


def run(binary, args):
    p = subprocess.run([binary] + args, capture_output=True)
    return p.stdout, p.returncode, p.stderr


def main():
    executed = 0
    skipped = 0
    mismatches = []
    stderr_notes = []

    for tag, args in gen_cases():
        if any(b"\x00" in a for a in args):
            skipped += 1
            continue
        try:
            c_out, c_rc, c_err = run(CPP, args)
            r_out, r_rc, r_err = run(RUST, args)
        except (ValueError, OSError) as exc:
            skipped += 1
            print("SKIP %s: %r (%s)" % (tag, args, exc))
            continue
        executed += 1

        if c_out != r_out or c_rc != r_rc:
            # reproduce a second time before believing it
            c_out2, c_rc2, _ = run(CPP, args)
            r_out2, r_rc2, _ = run(RUST, args)
            stable = (c_out2 == c_out and r_out2 == r_out
                      and c_rc2 == c_rc and r_rc2 == r_rc)
            mismatches.append((tag, args, c_out, c_rc, r_out, r_rc, stable))
            print("=" * 70)
            print("MISMATCH [%s] stable_on_rerun=%s" % (tag, stable))
            print("  argv  : %r" % (args,))
            print("  repro : %s" % repro(args))
            print("  cpp rc=%d  out=%r" % (c_rc, c_out))
            print("  rust rc=%d out=%r" % (r_rc, r_out))
            sys.stdout.flush()
        if c_err != r_err:
            stderr_notes.append((tag, args, c_err, r_err))

    print("=" * 70)
    print("cases executed : %d" % executed)
    print("cases skipped  : %d" % skipped)
    print("mismatches     : %d" % len(mismatches))
    print("stderr diffs   : %d" % len(stderr_notes))
    for t, a, ce, re_ in stderr_notes[:10]:
        print("  STDERR-DIFF [%s] %r cpp=%r rust=%r" % (t, a, ce, re_))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

input.strategy:
Strategy "ace-prefix": programmatic differential fuzzing of /workspace/dataset/test11_executable (C++ ground truth) vs /output/test11 (Rust port), with every mutation built around the "xn--" ACE prefix. Driver written in perl (no python3 on this box) at /tmp/wf-fuzz-r1-3/fuzz.pl, /tmp/wf-fuzz-r1-3/round2.pl, /tmp/wf-fuzz-r1-3/round3.pl, /tmp/wf-fuzz-r1-3/round4.pl. Each case is passed as raw bytes in a SINGLE argv element via fork + `exec { $bin } ($bin, @args)` (list form, never a shell, never re-split); stdout and stderr are redirected to separate files in the child and compared with `cmp -s`; wait status is compared for both exit code and killing signal.

Harness was validated with controls first (/tmp/wf-fuzz-r1-3/sanity.pl): cpp-vs-cpp reports SAME, cpp-vs-/bin/echo reports DIFF (so the comparator can actually fail), /bin/false exit code is captured, and a raw 0xff byte survives the argv round-trip into the output.

Four rounds:
1. Round 1 (7032 cases): ~58 prefix variants (all case permutations of x/n crossed with 0-5 dashes; truncations "", x, X, n, N, -, --, ---; dash-displaced forms x-n--, xn.-, xn_-, xn -, xnn--, xn---x, nx--; near-miss bytes \xf8n--, x\xee--, xn\x2d\xad, en-dash and fullwidth "xn") crossed with 48 bodies, plus prefix-only, prefix+1char over 23 chars, repetition 1-8x for 7 flavours, embedding at every offset of 5 carriers, per-label templates (a.xn--b, xn--a.xn--b, xn--.a.xn--.b.xn--), trailing/leading dot runs 0-8, 63/255 length boundaries, exotic sequences (ZWSP, BOM, soft hyphen, overlong NUL, ideographic/fullwidth full stop, emoji, lone surrogate), and a full 1-255 single-byte sweep in 5 positions around the prefix.
2. Round 2 (4709 cases): huge inputs, exhaustive byte 1-255 as whole body after 13 prefix flavours, one argv holding all 255 non-NUL bytes, prefix repetition up to 4096 copies, upper-case prefix glued to high bytes (to exercise ::tolower on a negative char), exact thresholds 58-68 and 250-260, and 1-1024 argv elements.
3. Round 3 (190 cases): the exact MAX_ARG_STRLEN ceiling (131071-byte args, the largest that actually exec) plus total-ARG_MAX pressure spread over 2-32 args.
4. Round 4 (14792 cases): exhaustive enumeration of EVERY string over the ACE-relevant alphabets - {x,X,n,N,-,.} for all lengths 0-5, and {x,n,-,\xff} for all lengths 0-6. This proves the prefix detect/strip logic by exhaustion rather than sampling.

Plus 45 targeted exit-code probes with stdout as a pipe closed early by the reader.

input.notes:
MAIN RESULT: zero divergences on the ace-prefix angle. Under the comparison protocol specified for this task (input as a single argv element, stdout captured to files, compared with `cmp -s`, exit codes compared), all 26,723 systematic cases matched byte-exactly, including the round-4 exhaustive enumeration of every string over {x,X,n,N,-,.} up to length 5 and {x,n,-,\xff} up to length 6. The Rust port's prefix handling is byte-faithful: `strip_prefix(b"xn--")` in /output/src/idna/convert.rs matches the C++ `s.find("xn--") == 0 ? s.substr(4) : s` on every input I could construct, including the case-sensitivity (XN-- is NOT stripped), all truncations, and the empty string.

ABOUT THE ONE REPORTED DIVERGENCE - read this before treating it as an ace-prefix bug. It is real and fully deterministic, but it is NOT prefix-specific and does NOT appear under the file-redirect protocol:
  - It reproduces identically with a plain non-prefixed argument (20000 'a's, no "xn--"), so it is an I/O/runtime difference, not ACE-prefix logic. I used an xn-- argument only because that is the angle I was fuzzing.
  - With stdout redirected to a file (the protocol above), the same argv gives cpp=0, rust=0 and byte-identical 120040-byte stdout. The divergence needs stdout to be a pipe whose reader closes early AND output large enough that a second write() syscall happens after the close.
  - Mechanism: Rust's std runtime sets SIGPIPE to SIG_IGN before main, so the write returns EPIPE; /output/test11.rs lines 49-51 then swallow it (`if out.write_all(&line).is_err() { return; }`) and main falls off the end with status 0. The C++ binary keeps the default SIGPIPE disposition and is killed by signal 13. Whether this counts as a port defect is a judgement call for the reviewer; I am reporting it because exit-code comparison was explicitly in scope and it reproduced every single time.

HARNESS ARTIFACT, NOT A FINDING: round 2 logged 20 "stderr diffs", all in the `huge` tag. Cause is that arguments of >=131072 bytes exceed MAX_ARG_STRLEN, so `exec` fails with E2BIG before either binary runs, and perl's error text embeds the binary path, whose length differs ("/workspace/dataset/test11_executable" vs "/output/test11"). Neither program executed; stdout and wait status matched. Round 3 then confirmed the largest args that DO exec (131071 bytes) match cleanly. Outside those E2BIG cases, stderr was byte-identical (both empty) in every case; neither binary ever wrote to stderr, and neither ever crashed, hung, or produced a nonzero exit under file-redirected stdout.

DELIBERATELY NOT COVERED (for a later reviewer / other rounds):
  - Non-ACE angles: I did not systematically fuzz the length predicates (is_valid_domain 255 / is_valid_label 63) away from the prefix, the count_labels dot counter on dot-dense inputs unrelated to "xn--", or to_lower/normalize over non-prefixed text. I hit these incidentally as output fields on every one of the 26k cases, but they were not the mutation target.
  - NUL bytes inside an argument: impossible to pass through execve, so untestable via argv. 0 cases were actually skipped for this reason since my generators never emitted a NUL.
  - Locale effects on ::tolower: I only ran under the inherited default locale. Running with LC_ALL/LANG set to a non-C locale (e.g. tr_TR.UTF-8 or a single-byte 8-bit locale) could make the C++ `::tolower` fold bytes >=0x80 that the Rust `to_ascii_lowercase` leaves alone. This is the most promising untested lead I am aware of and I recommend it as a follow-up angle.
  - Multi-byte/UTF-8 semantic correctness of real punycode: irrelevant here, since both implementations are stub string concatenations rather than actual punycode codecs.
  - Environment-dependent behaviour other than the pipe case: no tests with stdout on a full filesystem, a non-blocking fd, or a tty.
  - I did not diff argv handling above 1024 arguments, nor total ARG_MAX exhaustion beyond ~100 KB spread across 32 args.
